bill.name: Proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States to provide that no person shall be elected to the office of the President more than three times (H.J. Res. 29)
bill.status: Introduced in House · Rep. Andrew Ogles · referred to House Judiciary on January 23, 2025

provisions.title: Proposed constitutional article
provisions.heading: Presidential election ceilings and ratification condition
provisions.quote: “No person shall be elected to the office of the President more than three times, nor be elected to any additional term after being elected to two consecutive terms, and no person who has held the office of President, or acted as President, for more than two years of a term to which some other person was elected President shall be elected to the office of the President more than twice.”
provisions.context: H.J. Res. 29 proposes one constitutional article rather than an ordinary statute. The official resolving formula, omitted from the supplied raw extraction, requires two-thirds of each House to concur before submission. After submission, the article becomes valid only if the legislatures of three-fourths of the States ratify it within seven years. On its own terms, the article states three prohibitions: a general ceiling of three presidential elections, a bar on any additional election after two consecutive elected terms, and a two-election ceiling for a person who held or acted as President for more than two years of another person's elected term. These are ceilings, not affirmative guarantees of eligibility. The proposal does not state how it interacts with existing constitutional presidential-term language or how elections and partial-term service before ratification would count.
goals: Set a constitutional ceiling of three elections to the office of President.
Bar any additional presidential election after a person has been elected to two consecutive terms.
Set a two-election ceiling for a person who has held or acted as President for more than two years of a term to which someone else was elected.

effects.text: Introduction alone changes no constitutional rule. The proposed article would become valid only if the legislatures of three-fourths of the States ratify it within seven years after its submission for ratification.

If the article becomes valid, its first clause would prohibit any person from being elected President more than three times; a ceiling does not itself guarantee that any person is otherwise eligible or will seek or win another term.
The second clause would impose a separate and potentially stricter limit by prohibiting any additional election after a person has been elected to two consecutive presidential terms.
The third clause would prohibit a person who held or acted as President for more than two years of another person's elected term from being elected President more than twice.

barriers.text: The analyzed version is introduced and referred, not submitted for ratification. The official resolving formula requires two-thirds of each House to concur before submission, after which three-fourths of State legislatures must ratify before the seven-year deadline.

The proposal does not expressly repeal or amend existing constitutional presidential-term language and supplies no transition rule for elections or partial-term service before ratification. If the article becomes valid and those questions matter to a candidacy, they would require legal interpretation before eligibility could be administered.
